ui.n1: Colony on Pontes-01b — the game goes on: build the base, send data to Earth and receive the crew ships.
ui.n2: Explore Earth: enter the city's 8 buildings, read the panels with real data and talk to the residents. The Explorer's Diary (J) earns extra budget to build the ship.
ui.n3: Pick any planet at Ponte-Alfa Station — even the wrong ones. Every trip burns fuel, oxygen, food and days, and teaches you why Pontes-01b is the best bet.
ui.n4: The game goes on after landing: install solar panels, water and a greenhouse, raise the tower, send data to Earth and light the beacon so the crew ships can land.
ui.n5: Chat (Enter): in multiplayer, talk to the other players; in solo, talk to the crew and Mission Control.
ui.n6: Everyone talks through the room chat and works together on the colony: each player walks the surface, builds and lights the beacon while the ships descend.

ui.s10: Because of Earth's imminent collapse, the planet's leaders joined together for human survival. Observatories around the world located the closest habitable planet: Pontes-01b, Earth's only hope.
ui.s11: You manage one of the hundreds of ships launched into space: its resources, its crew and the route. On the way: meteor showers, radiation, microgravity, scarcity and everyone's psychological strain on board.
ui.s13: Preparation — 30 budget points, 5 module slots. Every choice is a sacrifice.
ui.s14: Departure and travel — fly the ship and face the first space problems.
ui.s16: The new world — investigate Pontes-01b and face adaptation.
ui.s17: Migration — decide where humanity will start over.
ui.s19: Before each challenge a warning shows the kind of problem, the parts involved and their damage level. Life-support numbers use public references (ISS): 0.84 kg of O₂ per person/day, up to 98% water recycling and oxygen electrolysis. The damage level shows the percentage of integrity lost each time it happens to that item: Low −10%, Medium −20%, High −30%.

ui.s51: Tends the garden and the food.
ui.s59: Walk around the ship in 2D side cutaway and use the stations (E): bridge, engines, radio, laboratory, infirmary, avionics, thermal panel, tanks, life support, greenhouse, kitchen, airlock and dormitories.
ui.s60: Quick look on the top bars; deep look in the Report (R), with the inflows and outflows of each resource.
ui.s61: Random challenges: thermal regulation, meteor showers, fuel shortage and leak, oxygen failure, crazy panel, trash, radio interference, contaminated water, suit leak, illness and solar storm.
ui.s62: Hidden rolls use d20 and d10. You get clues (a confident voice, a yellow light, a red light), not numbers.

falas._info: Falas do jogo Pontes01 (PT/EN/ES). Edite aqui os textos falados: narração, moradores, tripulação e Controle da Missão.
story: Because of Earth's imminent collapse, for a long time the planet's main leaders had been meeting for the sake of human survival.
Amid the chaos, observatories around the world joined forces to find the habitable planet closest to Earth. And they did.
Named “Pontes-01b”, it became Earth's only hope of survival.
You will manage one of the hundreds of stations and spaceships launched into space: its resources, its crew and the route to Pontes-01b.
During the expedition you will face asteroid showers, radiation, microgravity, scarce resources and everyone's psychological strain on board.

lia.name: Ms. Lia
say: Hey, you! Yes, you! Come closer, don't be afraid.
Look at this city: trash everywhere, burning air, 46 °C… They say they are enlisting people for Pontes-01b.
Rationing level 4… every drop counts. Did you see how astronauts recycle even their sweat?
Astronauts joke: “yesterday's coffee is tomorrow's coffee”. A joke from people who recycle ISS water!
Carry water in your heart, Commander.

teo.name: Professor Théo
say: As a kid I counted stars. Today we count planets: over 6,000 exoplanets are confirmed!
Not every “Earth-like” planet is good. Near red dwarfs, the star's flares can strip the atmosphere.
If one day at the station someone offers you a “perfect” planet… check the data before you accelerate!

mari.name: Mari
say: My teacher said astronaut Scott Kelly spent 340 days on the ISS and came back ~5 cm taller!
Without gravity the spine stretches. But it goes back to normal. I wish I could see stars without pollution…
Promise you'll send a photo of Pontes-01b?

ramos.name: Mr. Ramos
say: I watched the Perseverance Mars landing in 2021 on TV: the “7 minutes of terror” of the descent, all alone, with nobody on Earth able to help.
After that the Ingenuity helicopter flew 72 times on Mars, far more than the 5 planned. Good design leaves margin.
An old-timer's advice: bring spare parts!

bia.name: Bia
say: In space medicines also age faster because of radiation. The ship must renew its stock.
If someone gets nausea, headache or fever: measure, compare symptoms and only then pick the medicine.

gui.name: Gui
say: I write navigation software. One degree of error at departure becomes millions of km at arrival.
DSOC test sent laser video from 31 million km at 267 Mbps. Radio is the past!

nina.name: Professor Nina
say: On Earth the atmosphere regulates temperature for free. On a ship everything has a cost: heat only leaves by radiation.
That is why it is easier to keep Earth habitable than to inhabit another planet. Remember that out there.

beto.name: Tio Beto
say: Potato, soy, lettuce, chile… Lettuce grows in 4 days, potato takes longer but yields more. Planning the garden is planning the trip.
Oh! And don't forget the crew's allergies. Soy for someone allergic? No way.

crew.c2: Didn't get it the first time, trying again...
crew.c4: Speed is dropping! The main tank is not feeding the engine.
crew.c5: The panel went crazy! The map says we are near Jupiter...
crew.c6: There's trash floating all over the ship! And I think something got into the engine.
crew.c7: The radio only crackles... we are getting pieces of a message from Earth.
crew.c8: My suit is leaking! I can't hold out much longer!
crew.c9: If the ship stays still, one side cooks and the other turns to ice. I can rotate it slowly, but that uses fuel.
crew.c10: Out here heat only leaves by radiation. If we don't open the radiators, it stays trapped.
crew.c11: The thrusters are making a strange noise... not sure they can keep spinning the ship for long.
crew.c12: Our instruments run hot. We can turn some off, but we lose data.
crew.c13: The crew is getting cold. If this goes on, the body loses energy and thinking gets worse.
crew.c16: The thruster jammed! The ship stopped spinning!
crew.c17: I feel better, heading back to my post.
crew.c18: I'm having a strong allergic reaction...
crew.c19: I think I ate something that made me sick.
crew.c20: I'm weak... I'm going to faint.
crew.c21: Commander, the medicine batch expired. We need to replace it.

nasa: Mission Control: Earth's atmosphere now holds over 420 ppm of CO₂, versus ≈ 280 ppm before the industrial era.
Mission Control: Earth's average temperature has risen ≈ 1.2 °C since the late 1800s; the 10 warmest years on record are the last 10.
Mission Control: satellites show sea level has risen about 10 cm since 1993, and the pace is accelerating.
Mission Control: the ISS circles Earth every ~90 minutes at 28,000 km/h. Astronauts see 16 sunrises a day!
Mission Control: an astronaut breathes about 0.84 kg of oxygen a day. On the ISS, O₂ comes from splitting water by electrolysis.
Mission Control: in space there is no air to spread heat — a ship cools only by radiating. The sun–shade difference can top 200 °C.
Mission Control: a radio signal from Mars takes 3 to 22 minutes to reach Earth. Live conversations are impossible!
Mission Control: the Kepler telescope (2009–2018) found over 2,600 planets by watching tiny dips in starlight (the transit method).
colonyFacts: Mission Control: on the ISS, astronauts lose 1–1.5% of bone mass per month in microgravity and exercise about 2 hours a day to reduce it.
Mission Control: an ISS astronaut gets about 80 mSv of radiation in 6 months; on Earth the natural average is ≈ 3 mSv a year.
Mission Control: Voyager 1, launched in 1977, travels at 17 km/s and is already about one light-day away. Even so, it would take ~75,000 years to reach the nearest star.
Mission Control: there are over 6,000 confirmed exoplanets in the Exoplanet Archive. Few lie in their star's habitable zone.
Mission Control: the James Webb telescope watches starlight pass through exoplanet atmospheres to learn which gases they contain.
Mission Control: recycle everything! On the ISS trash leaves on cargo ships that burn up on reentry; in a colony, waste is raw material.

comms.selected: You have been selected for a space mission to save the future of humanity.
comms.next: Next announcement: you have a limited budget to build an exploration ship.

completa.t: Full Journey: about 30 days of travel and 9 challenges. It all starts on Earth: explore the city and accept the mission.
Build the ship with 30 budget points and 5 module slots. You can't have everything: every choice is a sacrifice.
During the trip, walk around the ship and use the stations. Watch oxygen, hunger, mood and storage. The onboard computer (H) always shows the next step.
Halfway there is Ponte-Alfa Station: analyze real exoplanets and pick your destination — even the wrong ones.
In orbit around Pontes-01b: run analyses, face adaptation and choose where to land.
On the surface, build the colony, send data to Earth and receive the crew ships.

curta.t: Short Journey: about 12 days and 4 challenges — great for classes. Start in the city on Earth.
Build the ship on a limited budget: survival modules first!
Travel, solve the challenges and use ⏩ (Shift+S) to speed up time until the next event.
Reach Pontes-01b. Press H whenever you are unsure.

multi.t: Multiplayer: you are the Commander. Friends who join the room become crew members; empty seats go to bots.
Each player has a role: paramedic, navigator, farmer, two engineers and researcher. When a challenge calls your role, go to the station!
Plan everything in the room chat (Enter). Together you look after oxygen, hunger, mood and storage.
On Pontes-01b, everyone walks the surface, builds and lights the beacon so the ships can land.

paramedico: I'm watching everyone's health. Drink water and sleep well!
In microgravity bones lose mass. Remember to exercise!
navegador: The route is under control. Every degree of drift costs fuel.
The stars don't lie: Pontes-01b is right there.
agricultor: The plants are doing great! Lettuce in 4 days, potatoes take longer.
On the ISS they even harvested chile peppers. We'll have spice here!
eng: I can fix almost anything with a good part and a bit of power.
Systems are running. If anything beeps, I'll run!
pesquisador: The data we collect is gold for Earth.
Did you know there are over 6,000 confirmed exoplanets?
comandante: Commander here. We continue the mission.
